claim: Many PROTAC development campaigns fail because the selected E3 ligase candidates are unable to induce degradation of the particular target of interest.
source: Furthermore, many PROTAC development campaigns fail because the selected E3 ligase candidates are unable to induce degradation of the particular target of interest.
evidence: This is stated as a known problem in the field, supported by the discussion of empirical nature of PROTAC development.

claim: RiPA revealed that VHL, but not Cereblon, is able to induce WDR5 degradation.
source: Strikingly, this rapamycin-induced proximity assay (RiPA) revealed that VHL, but not Cereblon, is able to induce WDR5 degradation - a finding previously made by PROTACs, demonstrating its predictive power.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: The finding that VHL but not Cereblon degrades WDR5 was previously made by PROTACs.
source: Strikingly, this rapamycin-induced proximity assay (RiPA) revealed that VHL, but not Cereblon, is able to induce WDR5 degradation - a finding previously made by PROTACs, demonstrating its predictive power.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous PROTAC studies mentioned in the results section.

claim: About 80% of the intracellular proteome is undruggable by conventional inhibitors.
source: Thus, most of the existing therapies are so far directed against proteins with enzymatic activity, leaving about 80% of the intracellular proteome undruggable (Oprea et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Oprea et al., 2018.

claim: PROTACs are bifunctional small molecules which bind to their target and a cellular E3 ligase and induce target ubiquitylation and degradation.
source: PROTACs are bifunctional small molecules which bind to their target and a cellular E3 ligase and hence induce target ubiquitylation and degradation (Bondeson et al., 2015; Ishida and Ciulli, 2021; Winter et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a definition supported by multiple citations.

claim: Complete degradation by PROTACs results in the inactivation of any protein function, including all enzymatic activities in multi-enzyme proteins or non-enzymatic activities in enzymes with additional scaffolding functions.
source: First, complete degradation results in the inactivation of any protein function, such as all enzymatic activities in multi-enzyme proteins or non-enzymatic activities in enzymes with additional scaffolding functions.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of PROTACs based on logical inference about complete protein removal.

claim: PROTACs act more persistently and at lower drug concentrations than classical inhibitors because they remain active after inducing target degradation.
source: Second, because PROTACs remain active after once having induced the degradation of their target (=catalytic mode of action), they act more persistently and at lower drug concentrations, making them more specific than classical inhibitors (=occupancy-based mode of action) (Farnaby et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Farnaby et al., 2021.

claim: PROTACs are less susceptible to resistance-mediating mutations that reduce target affinity for the drug because transient ternary complex formation is sufficient to ubiquitylate the target.
source: Third, since the transient formation of the ternary complex of target, PROTAC, and E3 ligase is sufficient to ubiquitylate the target, PROTACs are less susceptible to the formation of resistance-mediating mutations that reduce the affinity of the target for the drug (Posternak et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Posternak et al., 2020.

claim: Numerous PROTACs are already in clinical development.
source: Therefore, despite its novelty, the PROTAC concept has transformed the development of targeted therapies, and numerous PROTACs are already in clinical development with the first cases of successful clinical trials recently being reported (Chirnomas et al., 2023; Montoya et al., 2024).
evidence: This is stated with citations to recent clinical trial reports.

claim: The first cases of successful PROTAC clinical trials have recently been reported.
source: Therefore, despite its novelty, the PROTAC concept has transformed the development of targeted therapies, and numerous PROTACs are already in clinical development with the first cases of successful clinical trials recently being reported (Chirnomas et al., 2023; Montoya et al., 2024).
evidence: This is stated with citations to Chirnomas et al., 2023 and Montoya et al., 2024.

claim: Most PROTACs are based on only two E3 ligases: Cereblon (CRBN) and von Hippel-Lindau tumor suppressor (VHL).
source: While the human genome encodes for more than 600 E3 ligases, only a few are used to develop PROTACs (Ishida and Ciulli, 2021), and most PROTACs are based on only two of them, Cereblon (CRBN) and the von Hippel-Lindau tumor suppressor (VHL).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Ishida and Ciulli, 2021.

claim: Both VHL and CRBN are commonly expressed in human tissues, preventing their use for tissue-specific degradation.
source: For example, both E3 ligases are commonly expressed in human tissues preventing their use for tissue-specific degradation.
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation of these E3 ligases.

claim: Both VHL and CRBN are not essential for many cells in the body, which could lead to rapid development of resistance if the E3 ligase machinery is silenced.
source: In addition, both are not essential for many cells in our body, which could lead to the rapid development of resistance if the respective E3 ligase machinery is silenced, e.g., in the context of an oncology application.
evidence: This is stated as a potential problem based on inference about resistance mechanisms.

claim: The development of PROTACs is largely empirical, with few generally applicable design rules.
source: A second major limitation is that the development of PROTACs is largely empirical, with few generally applicable design rules (Ward et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Ward et al., 2023.

claim: Many PROTAC development campaigns fail due to the inability to identify PROTACs that efficiently induce target degradation.
source: As a result, many PROTAC development campaigns fail due to the inability to identify PROTACs that efficiently induce target degradation, and in most cases, these results are not published.
evidence: This is stated as an observation about the field.

claim: A possible reason for frequent PROTAC failure could be the incompatibility of a particular E3 ligase with a given target.
source: A possible reason for this frequent failure could be the incompatibility of a particular E3 ligase with a given target.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis based on observations.

claim: Promiscuous kinase inhibitors exhibit very distinct degradation profiles when used as ligands for PROTACs, demonstrating that PROTAC-mediated degradation efficacy is not determined solely by target and E3 ligand affinity but by efficient ternary complex formation.
source: In fact, it has been observed that promiscuous kinase inhibitors exhibit very distinct degradation profiles when used as ligands for PROTACs, demonstrating that the efficacy of PROTAC-mediated degradation is not determined solely by the sheer affinity of the target and E3 ligand but rather by efficient ternary complex formation (Donovan et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Donovan et al., 2020.

claim: Cereblon-based PROTACs targeting Aurora A show remarkable specificity toward Aurora A despite the kinase inhibitor also binding Aurora B.
source: While the kinase inhibitor we used for PROTAC development also binds and inhibits the homologous enzyme Aurora B, our Cereblon-based PROTACs show remarkable specificity toward Aurora A (Adhikari et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Certain amino acids on the putative Cereblon interaction surface of Aurora A are not conserved in Aurora B, and mutation of these residues decreases PROTAC-mediated degradation of Aurora A.
source: We observed that certain amino acids on the putative Cereblon interaction surface of Aurora A are not conserved in Aurora B, and that mutation of these residues decreases PROTAC-mediated degradation of Aurora A, indicating that ternary complex formation is supported by direct interactions between Aurora A and Cereblon.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the authors' previous work.

claim: Cooperativity in ternary complex formation is relevant for PROTAC efficacy.
source: In line with our finding, the Ciulli lab demonstrated that cooperativity in ternary complex formation is relevant for PROTAC efficacy (Roy et al., 2019; Gadd et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with citations to Roy et al., 2019 and Gadd et al., 2017.

claim: Certain E3 ligases are better suited for specific targets than others.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that certain E3 ligases are better suited for specific targets than others.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on cited literature and the authors' observations.

claim: New ligands have been discovered for E3 ligases including IAPs, DCAF11, DCAF15, DCAF16, RNF4, RNF114, AhR, FEM1B, and KEAP1.
source: The problem that only certain E3 ligases can efficiently degrade a particular target protein is exacerbated by the rapid discovery of new ligands for additional E3 ligases (such as IAPs [Itoh et al., 2010; Demizu et al., 2016], DCAF11 [Zhang et al., 2021], DCAF15 [Han et al., 2017; Du et al., 2019], DCAF16 [Zhang et al., 2019], RNF4 [Ward et al., 2019], RNF114 [Spradlin et al., 2019; Luo et al., 2021], AhR [Ohoka et al., 2019], FEM1B [Henning et al., 2022], and KEAP1 [Konopleva et al., 2002; Wei et al., 2021; Pei et al., 2023]).
evidence: This is stated with multiple citations to the discovery of these ligands.

claim: Rapamycin induces dimerization of FKBP12 protein and FRB domain.
source: Here, we used the well-established dimerization of the FKBP12 protein and FRB domain by rapamycin to bring the target protein WDR5 into proximity with candidate E3 ligases.
evidence: This is stated as a well-established mechanism and is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Rapamycin induced a marked reduction in WDR5-FKBP12 when a 10- or 100-fold excess of VHL-FRB was expressed.
source: Immunoblotting showed that rapamycin induced a marked reduction in WDR5-FKBP12 when a 10- or 100-fold excess of VHL-FRB was expressed, but not when the target protein and E3 ligase were transfected at equimolar ratios (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Rapamycin did not induce WDR5-FKBP12 reduction when target protein and E3 ligase were transfected at equimolar ratios.
source: Immunoblotting showed that rapamycin induced a marked reduction in WDR5-FKBP12 when a 10- or 100-fold excess of VHL-FRB was expressed, but not when the target protein and E3 ligase were transfected at equimolar ratios (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: FRB alone did not decrease WDR5-FKBP12 levels, demonstrating that VHL causes degradation of WDR5-FKBP12 in response to rapamycin.
source: FRB alone did not decrease WDR5-FKBP12 levels, demonstrating that VHL causes degradation of WDR5-FKBP12 in response to rapamycin.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Rapamycin reduced luciferase activity by 50.2% (±5.8%) when WDR5-Luc-FKBP12 was expressed together with a 10- or 100-fold excess of VHL-FRB.
source: Strikingly, rapamycin reduced luciferase activity by 50.2% (±5.8 %) when expressed together with a 10- or 100-fold excess of VHL-FRB (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Both VHL-FRB and CRBN-FRB induced time-dependent degradation of Aurora A.
source: In contrast to WDR5, both E3 ligases induced a robust degradation of Aurora A as shown by immunoblotting (Figure 2C) and luciferase activity (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 2C and 2D.

claim: VHL-FRB induced robust and time-dependent degradation of WDR5, but CRBN-FRB did not.
source: Both immunoblotting and luciferase assays again revealed a robust and time-dependent degradation of WDR5 by VHL-FRB but not by CRBN-FRB (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 2A and 2B.

claim: Several studies with PROTACs indicate efficient degradation of WDR5 by VHL but not by CRBN.
source: This is relevant because several studies with PROTACs indicate efficient degradation of WDR5 by VHL but not by CRBN (Dölle et al., 2021; Yu et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated with citations to Dölle et al., 2021 and Yu et al., 2021.

claim: CRBN-based PROTACs have been shown to efficiently degrade Aurora A.
source: In contrast, CRBN-based PROTACs have been shown to efficiently degrade the mitotic kinase Aurora A (Donovan et al., 2020; Adhikari et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2021; Rishfi et al., 2023; Liu et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated with multiple citations.

claim: Luciferase contains 7 lysine residues and FKBP12 contains 8 lysine residues.
source: In fact, luciferase and FKBP12 proteins contain 7 and 8 lysine residues, respectively.
evidence: This is stated based on analysis of protein structures shown in Figure 2E.

claim: All 15 lysine residues in luciferase and FKBP12 are located on the protein surfaces accessible for post-translational modifications.
source: Therefore, we analyzed the available crystal structures of both proteins and found that all 15 lysine residues are located on the protein surfaces accessible for post-translational modifications (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Lysine substitution to arginine in luciferase and FKBP12 reduced luciferase activity by 35.4%.
source: While lysine substitution reduced luciferase activity by 35.4%, the measurement of luciferase activity was still reliable (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Rapamycin-induced proximity to VHL induced WDR5 degradation comparable to lysine-containing protein tags when using lysine-less versions of luciferase and FKBP12.
source: Strikingly, rapamycin-induced proximity to VHL under these conditions induced WDR5 degradation comparable to lysine-containing protein tags (Figure 2G, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), demonstrating that VHL induces direct ubiquitylation of WDR5.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2G and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: VHL induces direct ubiquitylation of WDR5.
source: Strikingly, rapamycin-induced proximity to VHL under these conditions induced WDR5 degradation comparable to lysine-containing protein tags (Figure 2G, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), demonstrating that VHL induces direct ubiquitylation of WDR5.
evidence: This is concluded from the lysine-less experiment showing degradation still occurs.

claim: VHL was notably more effective than CRBN in degrading Aurora B.
source: While both VHL and CRBN exhibited comparable degradation efficiency against Aurora A, VHL was notably more effective than CRBN in degrading Aurora B (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: CRBN-harnessing degrader targeting oncogenic KRASG12C using a GFP-tagged KRASG12C reporter system failed to degrade endogenous KRASG12C, suggesting the degrader primarily ubiquitinated the GFP tag.
source: Previous work by Zeng et al. demonstrated that CRBN-harnessing degrader targeting oncogenic KRASG12C using a GFP-tagged KRASG12C reporter system failed to degrade the endogenous KRASG12C, suggesting that the degrader primarily ubiquitinated the GFP tag rather than the KRASG12C itself (Zeng et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Zeng et al., 2020.

claim: VHL-recruiting degraders efficiently degrade KRASG12D and other KRAS mutants compared to CRBN-recruiting degraders.
source: Other studies have consistently reported that VHL-recruiting degraders efficiently degrade KRASG12D and other KRAS mutants compared to CRBN-recruiting degraders (Zhou et al., 2024; Lim et al., 2021; Bond et al., 2020; Yang et al., 2022; Zhang et al., 2023; Yang et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated with multiple citations.

claim: VHL-FRB efficiently degraded KRASG12D in the RiPA system.
source: Consistent with these findings, our system demonstrated efficient degradation of KRASG12D by VHL-FRB.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Rapamycin-induced dimerization with CRBN-FRB only led to minor removal of KRASG12D.
source: In contrast, rapamycin-induced dimerization with CRBN-FRB only lead to minor target removal (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The presence of proteasomal inhibitor MG132 and neddylation inhibitor MLN4924 substantially blocked rapamycin-mediated depletion of KRASG12D by VHL-FRB.
source: The presence of both inhibitors substantially blocked rapamycin-mediated depletion of KRASG12D by VHL-FRB, confirming that target depletion was indeed due to proteasomal degradation (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: The RiPA system is capable of inducing target ubiquitylation and predicting suitable target/E3 ligase pairs.
source: We conclude that the RiPA system is capable of inducing target ubiquitylation and predicting suitable target/E3 ligase pairs.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data presented in the results section.

claim: The degradative function of E3 ligase FBXL12 was recently suggested by pooled genome-wide screens.
source: We chose the E3 ligase FBXL12 as a candidate because its degradative function was recently suggested by pooled genome-wide screens (Poirson et al., 2022), but had not been exploited by PROTACs.
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Poirson et al., 2022.

claim: FBXL12 had not been exploited by PROTACs prior to this study.
source: We chose the E3 ligase FBXL12 as a candidate because its degradative function was recently suggested by pooled genome-wide screens (Poirson et al., 2022), but had not been exploited by PROTACs.
evidence: This is stated as a fact about the state of the field.

claim: Incubation with rapamycin induced robust degradation of WDR5 by FBXL12 as assessed by immunoblotting and luciferase activity assays.
source: Incubation with rapamycin-induced robust degradation of WDR5 as assessed by immunoblotting and luciferase activity assays (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 3A and 3B.

claim: The position of the luciferase in the WDR5-FKBP fusion protein is irrelevant to its activity and degradation by FBXL12.
source: Similar to our observation with VHL, the position of the luciferase in the WDR5-FKBP fusion protein is irrelevant to its activity and degradation by FBXL12 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: FBXL12 exhibited strikingly superior activity compared to VHL in degrading WDR5.
source: A direct comparison of WDR5 degradation induced by FBXL12 and VHL showed a strikingly superior activity of FBXL12 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: FBXL12 exhibited comparable potency to VHL in targeting KRASG12D.
source: Conversely, FBXL12 exhibited comparable potency to VHL in targeting KRASG12D (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The cellular expression level of the WDR5 fusion protein declined with increasing linker length between WDR5 and FKBP12.
source: Immunoblots showed that the cellular expression level of the WDR5 fusion protein declined with increasing linker length (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The construct without any linker between WDR5 and FKBP12 is the best expressed and also degraded most drastically by FBXL12 upon addition of rapamycin.
source: Strikingly, the construct without any linker between WDR5 and FKBP12 is not only the best expressed but also degraded most drastically by FBXL12 upon the addition of rapamycin (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 3E and 3F.

claim: Both tight and more flexible arrangements between the target protein and the dimerization tag allow quantification of E3 ligase activity, but a seamless fusion shows the most efficient degradation.
source: We conclude that both tight and more flexible arrangements between the target protein and the dimerization tag allow quantification of E3 ligase activity, but that a seamless fusion shows the most efficient degradation, possibly mimicking the cooperativity of PROTAC-induced ternary complex formation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the linker length experiments.

claim: Rapamycin-mediated dimerization with FBXL12 induced a robust and durable degradation of WDR5, reaching a maximum after 5 hours.
source: Rapamycin-mediated dimerization with FBXL12 induced a robust and durable degradation of WDR5, reaching a maximum after 5 hr.
evidence: This is supported by kinetic measurement data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: RiPA is able to estimate the degradation of 'novel' E3 ligases and allows kinetic measurements in living cells.
source: We concluded that RiPA is able to estimate the degradation of 'novel' E3 ligases and allows kinetic measurements in living cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the FBXL12 experiments and kinetic measurements.

claim: Based on the Reactome Pathway and UniProt database, only about 40% of 600 or more E3 ligases annotated in the human genome are believed to be associated with ubiquitin-proteasome system.
source: In fact, based on the Reactome Pathway and the UniProt database, only about 40% of 600 or more E3 ligases annotated in the human genome are believed to be associated with ubiquitin-proteasome system (Schapira et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Schapira et al., 2019.

claim: All luciferase mutants except LucK12 are expressed to a level that allows robust measurements.
source: All luciferase mutants except LucK12, which contains 12 consecutive lysine residues in the peptide tail, are expressed to a level that allows robust measurements (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Luciferase versions with additional lysine residues on the cell surface (LucV1, LucV2) were degraded at the same rate and to a similar extent as wild-type luciferase by FBXL12.
source: We then co-expressed these mutants with FBXL12 and observed that the luciferase versions with additional lysine residues on the cell surface (LucV1, LucV2) were degraded at the same rate and to a similar extent as wild-type luciferase.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The additional lysines in LucK3 and LucK6 dramatically increased their degradation by FBXL12.
source: In contrast, the additional lysines in LucK3 and LucK6 dramatically increased their degradation by FBXL12 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: More than 60% of LucK6 is degraded 2 hours after the addition of rapamycin.
source: Kinetic measurements in living cells revealed that more than 60% of LucK6 is already degraded 2 hr after the addition of rapamycin (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by kinetic measurement data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Mutant versions of luciferase can be used as universal reporters to stratify E3 ligases in terms of their degradative potential.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrate that mutant versions of luciferase can be used as universal reporters to stratify E3 ligases in terms of their degradative potential.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the lysine-rich luciferase experiments.

claim: A growing body of literature indicates that often a specific E3 ligase cannot be used for PROTAC-induced degradation of a given target protein.
source: While PROTACs have revolutionized drug development, the design of such molecules, including the choice of appropriate E3 ligases, is still largely empirical (Bond and Crews, 2021). A growing body of literature indicates that often a specific E3 ligase cannot be used for PROTAC-induced degradation of a given target protein and that certain target/E3 ligase pairs are more suitable than others (Donovan et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2023; Yang et al., 2023; Steinebach et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated with multiple citations.

claim: RiPA can quantitatively measure the degradation of specific targets by E3 ligases when brought together.
source: Therefore, we developed a RiPA to quantitatively measure the degradation of specific targets by E3 ligases when brought together.
evidence: This is the main claim of the study supported by all experimental data.

claim: RiPA is in principle able to induce target degradation, as demonstrated by analyzing the degradation of WDR5 when brought into proximity with VHL.
source: First, we were able to show that RiPA is in principle able to induce target degradation by analyzing the degradation of WDR5 when brought into proximity with VHL.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data in the results section.

claim: The plasmid encoding the candidate E3 ligase must be transfected in at least 10-fold excess over the target protein-containing plasmid for efficient degradation.
source: We observed that the plasmid encoding the candidate E3 ligase must be transfected in at least 10-fold excess over the target protein-containing plasmid for efficient degradation.
evidence: This is based on the optimization experiments shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Both FRB and the minimal luciferase still function when all lysines are mutated to arginine.
source: Third, we observed that both, FRB and the minimal luciferase used for dimerization and detection of the target protein respectively, still function when all lysines are mutated to arginine.
evidence: This is supported by the lysine-less experiments shown in Figures 2F and 2G.

claim: RiPA only reports degradation of the target protein when it is directly ubiquitylated since ubiquitylation of the reporter can be excluded using lysine-less tags.
source: This ensures that RiPA only reports degradation of the target protein when it is directly ubiquitylated since ubiquitylation of the reporter can be excluded.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the lysine-less experiments.

claim: The lack of WDR5 degradation by Cereblon recapitulates experience with WDR5 and Aurora A PROTACs.
source: The lack of WDR5 degradation is not due to a general inability of Cereblon to induce protein degradation RiPA conditions, since Cereblon efficiently decreased Aurora A levels. This is noteworthy because it recapitulates our experience and that of others with the WDR5 and Aurora A PROTACs: while Cereblon-based PROTACs were able to efficiently degrade Aurora A (Donovan et al., 2020; Adhikari et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2021; Rishfi et al., 2023; Liu et al., 2022), they were either nonfunctional (Dölle et al., 2021) or much less potent (Yu et al., 2023; Yu et al., 2021) at degrading WDR5 compared to VHL-based PROTACs.
evidence: This is stated with multiple citations to PROTAC studies.

claim: A possible reason for the selective potency of VHL and CRBN to degrade WDR5 by PROTACs could be their different ability to bind to WDR5 through protein-protein interactions and thus support ternary complex formation.
source: A possible reason for the selective potency of both E3 ligases to degrade WDR5 by PROTACs could be their different ability to bind to WDR5 through protein-protein interactions and thus support ternary complex formation.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis based on structural studies.

claim: WDR5 could be co-crystallized with a variety of PROTACs and the respective E3 ligase, resulting in ternary complexes with a range of interface sizes between the two proteins.
source: Indeed, WDR5 could be co-crystallized with a variety of PROTACs and the respective E3 ligase, resulting in ternary complexes with a range of interface sizes between the two proteins.
evidence: This is stated as a fact from structural studies.

claim: The most potent WDR5 PROTACs induced the largest interaction area between WDR5 and E3 ligase, underlining the importance of achieving extensive protein-protein interactions for efficient target degradation.
source: The most potent PROTACs, however, induced the largest interaction area, underlining the importance of achieving extensive protein-protein interactions for the most efficient target degradation (Schwalm et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Schwalm et al., 2023.

claim: WDR5 degradation decreased in the RiPA setting as the linkers between WDR5 and FKBP12 became longer.
source: Strikingly, WDR5 degradation also decreased in the RiPA setting as the linkers between WDR5 and FKBP12 became longer, with the WDR5-FKBP12 construct without any linker being the most efficient.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 3E and 3F.

claim: RiPA closely recapitulates the E3 ligase selectivity of WDR5 PROTACs.
source: We conclude that RiPA closely recapitulates the E3 ligase selectivity of WDR5 PROTACs and hypothesize that it can, in principle, predict E3 ligases capable of forming ternary complexes with specific target proteins.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparison of RiPA results with PROTAC literature.

claim: RiPA can predict E3 ligases capable of forming ternary complexes with specific target proteins.
source: We conclude that RiPA closely recapitulates the E3 ligase selectivity of WDR5 PROTACs and hypothesize that it can, in principle, predict E3 ligases capable of forming ternary complexes with specific target proteins.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis based on the experimental results.

claim: FBXL12 can degrade artificial substrates in the context of the RiPA system.
source: Another finding of our study is that the SCF (SKP1-CUL1 F-box protein)-type FBXL12 can degrade artificial substrates in the context of the RiPA system.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data with FBXL12.

claim: FBXL12-mediated degradation of WDR5 is even more efficient than degradation by Cereblon.
source: Since FBXL12-mediated degradation of WDR5 is even more efficient than degradation by Cereblon, and since FBXL12 can induce degradation of every target protein tested in our study, our data suggest that FBXL12 may be a promising new E3 ligase for PROTAC development.
evidence: This is based on comparison of degradation data.

claim: FBXL12 can induce degradation of every target protein tested in the study.
source: Since FBXL12-mediated degradation of WDR5 is even more efficient than degradation by Cereblon, and since FBXL12 can induce degradation of every target protein tested in our study, our data suggest that FBXL12 may be a promising new E3 ligase for PROTAC development.
evidence: This is based on the experimental data with FBXL12 against multiple targets.

claim: FBXL12 may be a promising new E3 ligase for PROTAC development.
source: Since FBXL12-mediated degradation of WDR5 is even more efficient than degradation by Cereblon, and since FBXL12 can induce degradation of every target protein tested in our study, our data suggest that FBXL12 may be a promising new E3 ligase for PROTAC development.
evidence: This is stated as a suggestion based on the experimental results.

claim: Suitable target/E3 ligase pairs can fail in the RiPA setting because protein tags interfere with their interaction or reduce the activity of the E3 ligases.
source: Thus, suitable target/E3 ligase pairs can fail in the RiPA setting because protein tags interfere with their interaction or reduce the activity of the E3 ligases.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the system.

claim: An E3 ligase that can efficiently decrease the levels of a particular target in the RiPA setting may be less suitable for PROTACs if PROTACs that mimic the steric interaction of the target/E3 pair cannot be easily identified in the chemical space.
source: Conversely, it is also conceivable that an E3 ligase that can efficiently decrease the levels of a particular target in the RiPA setting may be less suitable for PROTACs, since PROTACs that mimic the steric interaction of the target/E3 pair may not be easily identified in the chemical space.
evidence: This is stated as a potential limitation.

claim: The RiPA system can identify inappropriate E3 ligases that are not in the same cellular compartment as the target or that cannot add a degradation-inducing ubiquitin chain.
source: However, the RiPA system can certainly identify inappropriate E3 ligases that are not in the same cellular compartment as the target or that cannot add a degradation-inducing ubiquitin chain.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of the system based on its design.

claim: RiPA correctly predicted the differential suitability of VHL and Cereblon to degrade WDR5.
source: Since RiPA also correctly predicted the differential suitability of VHL and Cereblon to degrade WDR5, we anticipate that it will be very helpful in streamlining chemical efforts in PROTAC development campaigns, both for PROTACs based on established and novel E3 ligases.
evidence: This is based on the comparison of RiPA results with PROTAC literature.

claim: RiPA will be helpful in streamlining chemical efforts in PROTAC development campaigns.
